doc.title: Scott Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe,Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: Advice to young players and closing
summary: He advises listening above all, and the interview ends with thanks.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: All right. Well I know that you’ve got to report downstairs and see what their schedule’s like.
Yeah. I’m guessing we’re still pretty far behind.
What do you think about advice to a seventeen year old aspiring jazz musician these days.

Listen. That’s my advice. Listen. And everything else grows out of that. You know if you listen to great music, you’ll get excited about it, you’ll get ideas, you’ll start wanting to transcribe, you’ll start wanting to learn those tunes, you’ll start wanting to figure out, how do they get that kind of sound out of the horn, that sound is like – you know, and you start fooling around. And you start thinking, well maybe I could write something, or maybe I could start a group and so you start writing and composing. Everything comes out of listening. That’s how it starts. You hear music, I mean, and you go wow — is it possible that maybe I could actually do that someday? Is that possible? And you start trying to find out. I’m still trying to find out.

Well I think you’re searching pretty well. And I wish you the best of luck with your new recordings with Frank Wess which I’m sure is a real gas, and everything else that you manage to do. Thanks for sharing your time, on behalf of Hamilton College.
Thanks, Monk. All right. Thank you. © Hamilton Fillius Archive -13-
